studied: naushemian.com — SUBSTITUTED. The assigned host naumanarfeen.com does NOT resolve (see notes); naushemian.com is the same designer's live storefront and is what every field below describes.
khaadi.com — real storefront is pk.khaadi.com (Salesforce Commerce Cloud / Demandware, NOT Shopify)

diagnosis: THE PHOTOGRAPH IS SUPPRESSED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE CLIENT'S 'MORE RELEVANT PICTURES' COMPLAINT. kj-v2.css:301 sets .lada__hero img{opacity:.55} and :310 lays a gradient over it — linear-gradient(to top, ground 3%, rgba(14,14,15,.55) 45%, rgba(14,14,15,.78) 100%). Net: the only Lada photograph on the page renders at roughly a quarter strength. Not one site in the study set does this. sanasafinaz, mariab.pk, naushemian and khaadi run ZERO scrim over the hero plate; amiradnan applies 0.2 black on one slide of four; HSY's is a flat 0.3. The picture may well be relevant — you cannot see it well enough to judge.

THE SCRIM IS ALSO POINTING THE WRONG WAY. The hero is align-items:flex-end (:299) so all type sits at the bottom, but the gradient is darkest at the TOP (.78 at 100%) and nearly clear where the type actually is (ground only at 3%). The 78% of black is spent on empty sky and the eyebrow/lede sit over the brightest part of the frame. sapphire is flagged in its own teardown for depending on a fragile per-slide text-shadow; this is the same class of error with the opposite geometry.

THERE IS EXACTLY ONE LADA PHOTOGRAPH IN THE REPOSITORY. theme/assets/lada-waistcoats.jpg, 1000x1250, 115KB — and it is simultaneously the hero of /pages/lada AND the background of lada-band on the homepage. The three lada-craft blocks expose image pickers and ship no images; lada-collection renders its empty state because the 13 draft products have no images. Against ismailfarid's 3,393-image enforced spec, sanasafinaz's 1,112 images at 99.3% single-ratio compliance and naushemian's 500x750 Photon ladder, Lada is a one-picture brand page. No layout change fixes this; only a shoot does.

THAT ONE PICTURE IS DECLARED WRONG IN THE MARKUP. lada-hero.liquid hard-codes width="2400" height="1500" — an 8:5 landscape intrinsic hint — on a 4:5 portrait 1000x1250 file, then requests image_url: width: 2400, a 2.4x upscale, and pours it into a clamp(520px,90svh,900px) landscape frame with object-fit:cover so the portrait is centre-cropped top and bottom. Wrong ratio hint means layout shift. khaadi is flagged for the same species of error (serving its 1920x700 desktop banner under max-width:1024px); amiradnan for the single-ratio-at-both-breakpoints version (90vh desktop, 26vh letterbox on mobile).

THE PRODUCT GRID IS A LIGHT-THEME CARD DROPPED ON A DARK GROUND — the one section that has to sell is the one section that is not on-brand. lada-collection.liquid renders the shared snippets/product-card.liquid, whose styles resolve against the house-of-brands light palette: .pcard__media{background:var(--surface)} = #FAF8F6, a near-white placeholder rectangle sitting on #0E0E0F while images load or when a product has none (which is all of them today); .pcard__meta and .pcard__price s at --text-tertiary #6B615A on #0E0E0F is about 2.6:1, below the 4.5:1 floor — the same failure ismailfarid is called out for at #AFAFAE-on-white (2.2:1); .pcard__quick is rgba(var(--bg-rgb),.96) with color:var(--text), i.e. a white slab with near-black text; and hover, sale badge and sale price all resolve to --accent/--sale #9A1B2F, a crimson that exists nowhere in the fixed Lada register.

HALF THE PAGE ARGUES FOR A DIFFERENT PRODUCT THAN THE ONE IT SELLS. The hero CTA reads 'The unstitched flagship', the grid heading is 'Lada, unstitched', the lede is 'Spun, woven and finished under our own roof', seal 1 is 'Every metre from our own looms', and lada-promise is a Lada-cloth-versus-sourced-cloth comparison ('We choose the yarn count', 'Mill sets the finish, we inspect every bolt'). Lada is eastern waistcoats and coats cut in Sheikhupura. Only lada-sizing (38R-46R) and the third seal are talking about garments. This is not a UI bug, but it is why the UI reads as unfocused — the sections are answering two different briefs.

TRUST FURNITURE IS COMPETING WITH THE PLATE. One 90svh viewport carries an eyebrow, the mark, a lede, two buttons and three seals — six content types. republicwomenswear's entire homepage has 'no testimonials, no USP/shipping icon strip, no press logos'; ismailfarid puts its four store addresses in the FIRST footer block, ahead of the newsletter; khaadi's three-cell service strip is an 80px band near the bottom of the page. The seals are Lada's real differentiators and belong on the page — just not on the photograph.

TRACKING IS SPRAYED, NOT HOARDED. The Lada block ships seven distinct letter-spacing values — .36em (eyebrow), .32em (kicker), .28em (stage number), .26em (seal dt), .24em (table th), .22em (button), .16em — and no element at 0. ismailfarid's teardown is explicit that hoarding tracking is what makes the two tracked elements read as deliberate; mariab runs h1-h5 at letter-spacing:0 flat. Lada currently has nothing untracked to contrast against, so none of it reads as a decision.

THE RANGE IS THE THIRD THING ON THE PAGE. Order is hero -> craft -> collection, so a visitor who came for a waistcoat scrolls a 90svh poster and then a three-column essay before seeing a garment. amiradnan's collection template renders no title and no banner at all so the first product image starts at 37.2vh; republicwomenswear's collection landing is nothing but a 3-up image wall starting at y=145. Product first, chrome second.

DECORATIVE MOTION WHERE THE SET SPENDS NONE. .lada__hero img runs a 22s scale(1.06)->scale(1) push-in. Not one of the nine sites animates its hero plate: mariab, khaadi, sanasafinaz and naushemian all hold a still image, and sanasafinaz's entire motion budget is four tokens capped at .5s. The set spends its motion on card hover (ismailfarid's 2s overshoot curve, sapphire's 2s scale to 1.09) and on scroll reveal, never on the plate.

FOUR CHEAP THINGS THE WHOLE SET HAS AND THIS PAGE DOES NOT: a stated lead time (HSY publishes 5-12 weeks couture against 4-6 weeks RTW; ismailfarid drives 7-8 / 20-25 / 25-30 days off product tags; naushemian states 12-15 days as a feature); fabric trade name separated from actual composition (khaadi shows 'Material: Raw Silk' above 'Fabric Composition: 70% Viscose 30% Polyester'); model height and size worn (sapphire prints both on every PDP, amiradnan burns 'Height 5'11", Size S' into the photograph); and a cloth-or-cut line on the card (khaadi's 'Embroidered | Raw Silk' eyebrow, where both halves are also real filter dimensions).

section_order.name: lada-hero
section_order.purpose: One still photograph, one name, one route in. Establish that this label is Khan Jee's own and get the visitor moving, without spending the whole first screen on a poster.
section_order.content: Eyebrow 'Woven and cut in-house · Est. 1978' (11px/600/0.24em caps, champagne). The mark as artwork, unchanged, as the page's only h1 with its real screen-reader label. ONE line of lede, max 16 words, rewritten to garments: 'Eastern waistcoats and coats, cut in our own workshop in Sheikhupura.' ONE primary button, 'See the range' -> #lada-collection. Delete the ghost second button (secondary route moves into the band below). Delete the three seals from this section entirely. Delete the 22s zoom; keep the existing prefers-reduced-motion block. Height clamp(460px,66svh,720px) so the proof band's top edge is visible above the fold. Scrim inverted: a single bottom-anchored gradient, rgba(14,14,15,.72) at 0% rising to transparent by 55%, and image opacity back to 1. Header transparent over the plate, --header-content-color set to --lada-bone for this template only, solid --lada-ground on scroll.
section_order.imagery: hero-plate-desktop and hero-plate-mobile — two separately shot files, not one file re-cropped.
section_order.why: Under-filling the fold is khaadi (58.8vh, hero bottom at y=640, 260px of the next section already legible) and ismailfarid (61.3%, 248px of the category row visible) — their teardowns both read the under-fill as confidence, 'a catalogue index rather than a poster'. Keeping live HTML copy is against 7 of 9 sites and deliberate: mariab's own teardown says it outright — zero words works for a house whose name is already known, and a new label cannot afford a silent first viewport. Two separately art-directed crops is ismailfarid (1440x551 desktop + 640x960 mobile as distinct uploads), khaadi (1920x700 triptych + a different 1000x1500 portrait) and sapphire (2:1 + 4:5 via <picture><source media>). Killing the plate animation follows all nine.

section_order.name: lada-proof
section_order.purpose: Rehouse the three seals — in-house, unconditional guarantee, cut to measure — where they can be read instead of competing with the photograph.
section_order.content: A hairline band on --lada-panel directly under the hero. Three columns, no icons, no boxes, no shadows: dt at 11px/600/0.24em caps champagne, dd at 13px/300/1.7 bone-muted at a contrast-corrected value (see typography). 1px --lada-line rule above and between. Rewrite dd copy to garments and add the numbers: 'Cut in our own workshop in Sheikhupura', 'Replaced or refunded, no conditions, no time limit', '38R to 46R as standard, measured in the shop at no charge'.
section_order.imagery: None. This band is drawn in lines and type only.
section_order.why: khaadi's PDP information architecture is 'drawn entirely with lines' — 1px hairlines with +/- indicators, no card, no shadow, no fill — and that is what makes its chrome read as premium next to a mass-market engine. Putting the claims in plain text one band down rather than on the plate is ismailfarid (stores as the FIRST footer block, before the newsletter) and republicwomenswear (two named addresses, landlines and separate weekday/Sunday hours as flat footer text). republic also proves the negative: its homepage carries no USP icon strip at all.

section_order.name: lada-collection
section_order.purpose: The range, promoted from third to third-thing-you-see, as a silent wall of photographs.
section_order.content: Kicker 'The range', h2 'Waistcoats and coats'. Above the grid, a single scrollable row of sub-category pills — All / Waistcoats / Prince coats / Made to measure — 0 radius, 1px --lada-line, filling to --lada-panel on hover. NO filter rail, NO sort dropdown, NO result count. Grid 2-up mobile / 3-up tablet / 4-up desktop at 4:5, column-gap var(--s4), row-gap var(--s8) so the vertical gutter is roughly 4x the horizontal. FORK the card for this ground: build snippets/lada-product-card.liquid rather than restyling the shared .pcard, because product-card.liquid carries the white-label vendor rule that Lada does not need. Card carries exactly four things — 4:5 primary image, a cloth-and-cut eyebrow ('Boski | Band collar', 11px/400/0.16em caps, muted), a proper piece name (15px/500 sentence case, bone), and the price (15px/500 tabular, bone, never larger than the title, never coloured). Made-to-measure pieces show 'Measured in the shop' in the price slot, linking to #lada-measure. No SKU on the card. No badge. No swatch. No rating. No compare-at price, ever. Placeholder box background must be --lada-panel, not --surface. Keep the existing empty state but rewrite it to garments.
section_order.imagery: card-primary and card-hover per piece, plus one macro per piece for the PDP.
section_order.why: Product-first ordering is amiradnan (empty collection header, first image at 37.2vh, SEO prose exiled below pagination) and republicwomenswear (collection landing is a bare 3-up image wall from y=145). The four-element card is the strongest agreement in the set: republic's card has literally two children under the image, ismailfarid's has three, naushemian's has image+caps title+price, and all three grep-verify zero badges, zero ratings, zero swatches. The cloth|cut eyebrow is khaadi's 'Embroidered | Raw Silk' — its teardown calls it the strongest single idea on the site because the card teaches the filter vocabulary while you browse. Proper piece names over descriptor-SKUs is HSY (Zafraan, Shamsher, Nawab-e-Zar) against naushemian's flagged failure ('SEQUINS EMBELLISHED MENS WAISTCOAT – NA-WC130') and mariab's flagged barcode under the H1. Row-gap far exceeding column-gap is mariab (20px column, 96px row, 4.8x) so rows read as spreads rather than a stock table. No facets is a scale call: republic, ismailfarid and HSY are all criticised for shipping none, but at 5-13 pieces a facet drawer is furniture pretending to be depth — revisit above about 30 SKUs and then copy khaadi's inline 300px rail that reflows the grid rather than covering it, with live counts and Show More at 6 values.

section_order.name: lada-craft
section_order.purpose: The in-house story, as process photography rather than more garment shots. This is the section that earns the price.
section_order.content: Keep the three-stage structure and the existing block schema. Retitle to garment making — Cut / Sew / Finish — and rewrite the body copy from cloth to construction: the pattern and the chalk, the machinist and the seam, the pressing and the lining. Numerals stay ('01 · CUT'). Add one named human: a first-person line signed by the owner, 14px/300 italic, and credit the karigars by name if they consent. Images at 4:5 above each stage, 1px --lada-line above each column as now.
section_order.imagery: craft-cut, craft-sew, craft-finish — three workshop frames, no model, no garment hero.
section_order.why: Founder voice in the first person on the landing page is HSY (a multirow section signed 'Hassan Sheheryar Yaseen'). Naming the makers is naushemian's lookbook intro, which credits model, photographer and 'karigars' by handle and name. Both earn provenance that a photograph of a finished coat cannot. The set's gap is instructive: naushemian is called out for shipping only 2 gallery images on a Rs.95,000 made-to-order garment with 'no detail or fabric macro to evidence the embroidery being sold', and neither amiradnan nor ismailfarid nor sanasafinaz shoots process at all. A working Sheikhupura floor is the one asset none of them has.

section_order.name: lada-lookbook
section_order.purpose: Answer 'more relevant pictures' with a run of full-bleed editorial frames that carries no commerce furniture at all — and quietly makes some of them shoppable.
section_order.content: Six to nine frames, full-bleed edge to edge, no captions, no prices, no add-to-cart, no badges, no hotspots. Alternate six 2:3 portraits with two 3:2 landscapes for rhythm. Vertical scroll-snap (scroll-snap-type: y proximity on the container, scroll-snap-align: start on each frame) — never wheel capture. Wrap three of the frames in a bare <a href> to the matching product, with no visible affordance beyond cursor:pointer. Any narrative copy goes BELOW the last frame, not between frames. Section padding 0, sections butt directly against their neighbours.
section_order.why: This is naushemian's /farhaad-2026 lookbook almost exactly: 41 frames at native resolution, zero prices, zero add-to-cart, zero captions, narrative parked at byte 103k of 105k — and 6 frames quietly wrapped in <a href="/product/…"> so the editorial converts without ever looking like a shop. The 2:3 portrait plus 3:2 landscape mix is their 33/8 split. Zero-padding full-bleed sections butting together is sanasafinaz (--spacing-sections-desktop: 0.0rem) and sapphire (measured 0px between all six homepage sections, 2px image gutters), both of which read as one continuous photographic surface rather than a stack of cards. Scroll-snap instead of Swiper wheel capture is sanasafinaz's own teardown recommendation against itself: releaseOnEdges:false breaks find-in-page, deep-linking and keyboard users.

section_order.name: lada-measure
section_order.purpose: Sell the measurement service as a service. This is Lada's single strongest differentiator and it is currently a paragraph inside a size table.
section_order.content: Two columns on --lada-panel. Left: h2 'Measured in the shop, at no charge', three numbered steps (come in or send measurements; we cut to them; collect or we courier), and the lead time stated plainly as two flat lines, not in an accordion: 'Standard 38R-46R — ready in 3 to 5 days' / 'Cut to your measurement — 10 to 14 days'. Right: one landscape photograph plus a primary button 'Send your measurements on WhatsApp' with pre-filled text, and a secondary text link 'Or visit the shop' -> #lada-house. No form, no Calendly.
section_order.why: Lead time published as a virtue and tiered by price is HSY (5-12 weeks couture against 4-6 weeks RTW, stated without apology) and ismailfarid (tag-driven 7-8 / 20-25 / 25-30 days, which doubles as a made-to-order signal). Stating it as two flat lines directly under the CTA rather than burying it in an accordion is republicwomenswear ('Local Delivery: 3 to 5 Working Days' / 'International: 8 to 10'). Made-to-order as a feature rather than an apology is naushemian ('My Custom Size' plus a free-text measurements field, an explicit 12-15 day lead time, disclaimers about peak wedding season). Routing to a human is ismailfarid, republic and HSY, all three of which run a persistent WhatsApp launcher; HSY's cards make 'Price on Request' itself the wa.me link on 16 of 16 menswear cards. What NOT to copy: HSY sells a 60-minute Calendly appointment because it is a couture atelier — Khan Jee is a shop with a counter, so the door and the WhatsApp number are the offer.

section_order.name: lada-sizing
section_order.purpose: Keep the real garment table. Make it reachable from the point of doubt rather than only from a page scroll.
section_order.content: Keep the 38R-46R table and the four how-to-measure lines. Widen the table to the columns the set actually uses: Size / Chest / Waist / Length / Shoulder / Collar, in inches, tabular-nums, hairline rules only. Add an INCHES / CM toggle. Beside it, a 1px champagne line drawing of a waistcoat with the six measurement points called out. Then expose this same table as an inline popover from a 'Size guide' link sitting immediately beside the size selector on the PDP — same markup, two entry points.
section_order.why: A real garment measurement table in inches is naushemian (Size / Length / Chest / Tummy / Hips / Shoulders / Collar, S through XL) and sapphire (7 measurements across 5 sizes with an INCHES/CM tab pair and a technical line drawing beside it) — sapphire's teardown calls this the correct model for eastern silhouettes where fit is cut-specific. Delivering it as a popup next to the size field is naushemian ('measurement help at the exact moment of doubt'); republic goes further with a per-SKU chart. The counter-examples are the argument: amiradnan has zero size-chart matches on the entire PDP and hides the guide in the footer, and ismailfarid has none either. Lada already has the table — it just needs the second entry point.

section_order.name: lada-promise
section_order.purpose: State the guarantee in plain language. Delete the cloth-versus-cloth comparison, which belongs to a different product.
section_order.content: Replace the two-panel comparison entirely. One centred block, max 48ch: the unconditional guarantee in one sentence, then three hairline-separated lines — what it covers, how long it runs, how to claim (walk in, or WhatsApp). No 'Lada vs sourced cloth' table. No badges, no seals, no icons. Then two native <details name="lada-info"> accordions, mutually exclusive with no JavaScript: 'Cloth and construction' (trade name and actual composition disclosed as separate visible fields) and 'Care'. Titles 12px/600, hairline rules, +/- indicators, closed by default.
section_order.why: Mutually exclusive accordions via the HTML name attribute, no JS, is mariab. Hairline accordion rules with +/- and no card or shadow is khaadi. Separating the fabric trade name from the honest fibre content, both visible — 'Material: Raw Silk' above 'Fabric Composition: 70% Viscose 30% Polyester' — is khaadi, and its teardown calls it a genuine trust device directly transferable to this kind of cloth story. The comparison table has to go because it is arguing about yarn count on a page selling coats; and because HSY's teardown warns that with price and spec both withheld there is no material cue anywhere in the grid — the fix is a cloth line on the card and a composition field on the PDP, not a debate panel.

section_order.name: lada-house
section_order.purpose: Physical proof. A named workshop and a door you can walk through, in plain text, at the bottom of the page.
section_order.content: Full-width band on --lada-ground, 1px --lada-line top. Left: 'Khan Jee Center, Civil Quarters Road, Sheikhupura. Est. 1978.' plus opening hours and a landline, as selectable text — not an image, not a map embed. Right: one photograph of the shopfront. Below, two routes split by intent: one WhatsApp number for orders and reservations, one for measurement and fit. One persistent WhatsApp launcher, bottom-right, champagne on ground, 0 radius, 44px minimum.
section_order.why: Physical retail as the trust signal is ismailfarid, whose footer's FIRST block is four named store addresses with landlines, ahead of the newsletter; republicwomenswear names two addresses with landlines, weekday and Sunday hours separately, and routes three different phone numbers by intent (online orders / studio appointments / bridal); naushemian lists a flagship studio and a factory outlet; HSY names 'HSY Mansion, 23-G, Ali Zaib Road, Gulberg-III, Lahore' with stated showroom hours. Four of nine assert the physical world in plain text and it is the highest-earning single move available to a 1978 Sheikhupura fabric house. The styling caveat is HSY's flagged failure: a teal #26a69a WhatsApp bubble at border-radius 2px dropped into an otherwise strict zero-radius black-and-white system. Ours must be champagne on ground at radius 0.

consensus: ONE LOCKED PORTRAIT PRODUCT RATIO, ENFORCED IN CSS, NEVER RE-CROPPED — 7 of 9. sanasafinaz: 1,070 of 1,112 images exactly 2:3, 1,033 of them exactly 1600x2400, 99.3% compliance, --ratio-percent:150%. mariab: 43/43 sampled at exactly 1600x2400. khaadi: 0.667 measured on both the 400x600 tile and the 800x1200 PDP frame, one master crop driven through ?sw=/&sh= transforms. republicwomenswear: 260 of 323 at exactly 1000x1231 (13:16), reused by card, PDP main, 63x77 thumbnail and the 1024x1024@2x lightbox. ismailfarid: 3,167 of 3,393 at exactly 1200x1580 (93.3%). naushemian: 500x750 from card to PDP to the whole Photon ladder. HSY: ~0.652 held across homepage, three collection pages and the couture PDP. What it earns: a grid that is visually silent because the assets are identical, and no ragged row bottoms. The failure case proves it — amiradnan pours 62% square and 37% 0.70 sources into one 2:3 card slot, so a third of the frame is centre-cropped off some cards and 5% off others.

MODEL ON LOCATION OR ON A BUILT SET. NEVER WHITE SWEEP, NEVER FLAT-LAY, NEVER GHOST MANNEQUIN — effectively 9 of 9. republicwomenswear: corner-pixel sampling across a 7-frame set returns RGB 19-45 on all four corners, a built textured-fibre wall with a bentwood chair; zero cutouts in the entire catalogue. khaadi: every single product image has a human in it, verified across homepage, PLP and PDP. ismailfarid: off-white waistcoat in open desert against blown-out sky, maroon waistcoat in an atelier of stacked painters' canvases, backgrounds always tonal and chosen to harmonise with the garment. naushemian and HSY: real architecture and interiors throughout. amiradnan: stone walls, palm and bamboo, arched architecture. What it earns: the photograph carries the premium signal so the interface does not have to.

THE CARD CARRIES ALMOST NOTHING, AND WHAT IT WITHHOLDS IS DELIBERATE — 9 of 9. republicwomenswear's .product-detail has precisely two children, an h2 and a price. ismailfarid's card is two stacked images, a centred title and a price, and its teardown notes the full variant JSON with every size and SKU is embedded in a data attribute on every card and never rendered — they built the data path for quick-add and chose not to use it. naushemian greps to zero for sale badges, star ratings, product labels, category links, swatches and quick-view, with countdowns hard-disabled in CSS. khaadi's colour-swatch CSS is fully written at three responsive sizes and never rendered. mariab: no swatches, no size list, no vendor, no stars, no second image. NOT ONE OF THE NINE SITES HAS A REVIEW OR RATING SYSTEM ANYWHERE — khaadi and mariab both load rating CSS on every card for a UI that never renders. What it earns: a resting grid that is pure photography.

EVERY TRANSACTIONAL AFFORDANCE IS HOVER-DEFERRED OR ABSENT — 6 of 9. sanasafinaz parks Quick Add at translateY(100%) below the image edge and the wishlist/quick-view rail at opacity 0 translate(.5rem). naushemian parks a 40px rgba(0,0,0,.9) action bar at bottom:-40px, visibility:hidden. amiradnan's Quick View sits at opacity 0 translateY(5px) inset 10px from the image edges. sapphire hides .addtocardbutton with display:none!important on the PLP entirely. mariab slides a white action bar from bottom:-15% to bottom:12px. What it earns: the photograph is never covered by commerce furniture at rest.

THE HOVER FRAME IS ANOTHER MODEL SHOT, NOT A DETAIL MACRO AND NOT A UI PANEL — 6 of 9. ismailfarid is the load-bearing example and its shot sequence is a system: frame 1 is a three-quarter crop from mid-thigh up, frame 2 is the full head-to-toe standing figure with feet near the bottom edge, so hover answers 'what does the whole thing look like on' — exactly the question a waistcoat shopper has. naushemian's .hover-img is 'always a second model frame, never a detail or flat'. amiradnan, khaadi, HSY and sanasafinaz all swap to a second on-model frame. What it earns: hover changes the information, not the decoration.

ZERO RADIUS AND NO SHADOW ON MERCHANDISING SURFACES — 5 of 9, and the two dissenters are the two the teardowns criticise. amiradnan: --buttonRadius:0 and --element-icon-radius:0, so buttons, inputs, size chips and image masks are all hard-cornered, and size selectors read as tailoring labels rather than UI pills. ismailfarid: 0px radius on Add to cart and on 42x42px size swatches. sanasafinaz: --product-card-corner-radius:0, --product-card-border-width:0, --media-radius:0px. HSY: --buttons-radius 0, --inputs-radius 0, every shadow token at 0.0. republic: 2px only. Lada's register already locks radius 0 — hold it.

SMALL TYPE. NOTHING SHOUTS — 7 of 9. republicwomenswear: nothing on the entire site exceeds 18px, the largest text being the PDP product name, with section headings at 13px and prices at 13px. amiradnan: the type scale caps at 32px and the single largest text anywhere is 38px, with section headings at Poppins 19px/weight 400/line-height exactly 1.0. naushemian: all eight homepage H2s at 22px. mariab: section h2 32px, product H1 only 20px. sanasafinaz: PDP h1 30px, card title 15px. sapphire: PDP product name 17px, tile name 11px. What it earns: all display scale is carried by the photography, and the words read as captions to it.

TRACKING IS RATIONED, NOT SPRAYED — 4 of 9 explicitly and it is the sharpest single typographic observation in the set. ismailfarid: zero on body, headings, product titles and prices, spent only on the collection H2 at 0.2em and spotlight titles at 0.08em — 'the restraint is what makes the two tracked elements read as deliberate'. sapphire: letter-spacing normal on the hero and all body copy, 4px reserved for 40-45px section headings only. republic: everything structural at +2px with one heading pushed to 16px on a 13px face. mariab: h1-h5 at letter-spacing 0 flat, line-height 100%. What it earns: tracked caps carry hierarchy instead of being ambient decoration.

MENSWEAR AND THE PREMIUM TIER ARE NEVER DISCOUNTED, AND DISCOUNT-LED PRESENTATION IS THE SET'S SINGLE LOUDEST 'AVOID' — 5 of 9 hold the line, 4 of 9 are criticised for breaking it. ismailfarid: compare_at_price is null across the entire eastern-wear range. mariab: menswear waistcoats sit at Rs.15,490-19,990 with compare_at_price 0.00 across the board while the womenswear grid is full of % OFF badges — its own teardown says copy that discipline, not the womenswear discount furniture. naushemian greps to zero for onsale. republic never shouts a discount: sale price in #000 and original struck in #858585 at identical size and weight, no percentage chip, no red, no SALE flag, and all 15 products on the measured page were marked down while the page still read as a lookbook. Against that: amiradnan carries a compare-at price on 227 of 250 sampled products with a 'Save 50%' amber label on 21 of 21 waistcoat cards; sanasafinaz's front door is 'DEFENCE DAY SALE / UP TO 50% OFF'; HSY's first element above the header is a bank promo reading 'Up to 50% off'; khaadi opens its filter rail on discount facets. What it earns: the price anchor the photography is working to build.

PHYSICAL AND HUMAN PROOF, IN PLAIN SELECTABLE TEXT — 4 of 9, and the highest-value move available to Lada. ismailfarid's footer's FIRST block is Stores: four addresses with landline numbers, ahead of the newsletter. republicwomenswear names two addresses with landlines, weekday and Sunday hours listed separately, and three phone numbers routed by intent. naushemian lists a flagship design studio and a factory care outlet. HSY names the atelier, a vanity number and 'Monday to Saturday, 11 AM to 7 PM (PST)'. What it earns: for a shop trading since 1978 on Civil Quarters Road, this is provenance no amount of art direction buys.

A REAL GARMENT MEASUREMENT TABLE IN INCHES, DELIVERED AT THE POINT OF DOUBT — 4 of 9, and the four absences are all flagged as failures. naushemian: Size / Length / Chest / Tummy / Hips / Shoulders / Collar, S through XL, in an inline popup triggered beside the size select. sapphire: 7 measurements across 5 sizes with an INCHES/CM tab pair and a garment line drawing. republic: a per-SKU chart named after the article code. khaadi: a Size Guide with a pencil icon beside the size chips. Against that, amiradnan has zero size-chart matches on the PDP with the guide exiled to the footer, and ismailfarid has none either. Lada already has the table.

LEAD TIME STATED AS A VIRTUE, TIERED BY PRICE — 4 of 9. HSY: couture 'Delivery Time — 5 to 12 weeks' against RTW '4 - 6 working weeks', the slower number belonging to the more expensive tier and stated without apology. ismailfarid: stored as a product tag (local_7 to 8 Working Days, international_10 to 12) and rendered into a PDP Shipping block, scaling from 7-8 days for ready-to-wear to 20-25 for ceremonial waistcoats. naushemian: an explicit 12-15 day bespoke lead time treated as a mark of craft. republic: two flat lines directly under the CTA rather than inside an accordion. What it earns: slowness reads as making rather than as delay.

MODEL HEIGHT AND SIZE WORN DISCLOSED — 3 of 9 but unanimous in intent and it answers the hardest question in online menswear. sapphire prints 'Model Height: 5 Feet 6 Inches' and 'Model Wears Size: S' in the PDP Description tab. mariab: 'Model is wearing medium size' inside its construction spec list. amiradnan burns 'Height 5'11"/155CM, Size S' into the photograph itself — a smart device, undermined only because it sits in the right third that the 2:3 card crop cuts off, so it survives on the PDP only. What it earns: de-risked fit without a returns culture.

THE HERO CARRIES NO HTML TEXT — 7 of 9, AND EVERY SINGLE TEARDOWN LISTS IT UNDER 'AVOID' FOR LADA. sanasafinaz: 0 words, 0 headings, 0 buttons across five panels. mariab: strip every tag from the hero and the only text left is the Swiper init script. naushemian: 33 slides, non-background layer count 0. khaadi: the hero markup is and nothing else. ismailfarid and amiradnan bake every word into the JPEG with alt="". HSY's 75vh video has empty heading, subheading and button slots and an empty aria-label. The consensus is real and the cost is unanimous: unselectable, untranslatable, invisible to search and to screen readers, re-typeset at whatever size the box happens to be, and a wording change needs a designer. This is the one place where following the set would be a mistake.
contested: HERO HEIGHT — 100vh versus deliberate under-fill. 100vh camp: sanasafinaz (exactly 100svh, header at 0px layout height, fold is 100.0% image, nothing below it teased), mariab (calc(100vh - 36px) with the header pulled on top), sapphire (measured 900/900). Under-fill camp: khaadi (58.8vh, hero bottom at y=640, 260px of the next section legible before any scroll, no vh unit anywhere in the CSS), ismailfarid (2.61:1 band at 61.3% of the fold leaving 248px of the category row visible), HSY (75vh). CALL: UNDER-FILL, clamp(460px,66svh,720px), with the proof band's top edge visible. Sana Safinaz and Maria.B. can spend an entire screen on a silent plate because the visitor already knows the house and is looking for this season's code — Lada is a label nobody has heard of with roughly five pieces. Khaadi's and Ismail Farid's under-fill is read in their own teardowns as confidence and as 'a catalogue index rather than a poster', which is precisely the register a small in-house menswear label wants. The current page is at clamp(520px,90svh,900px), which is the poster.

WORDS IN THE HERO — silent plate versus live HTML copy. Silent: 7 of 9 (sanasafinaz, mariab, naushemian, khaadi, ismailfarid, amiradnan, HSY). Live copy: sapphire only (six words in two uppercase lines plus one bare text CTA). CALL: LIVE HTML COPY, against the majority, and this is the current page's one genuinely correct decision. Maria.B.'s own teardown makes the argument better than I can: zero words works for a house whose name and season codes are already known, and a new label like Lada cannot afford a silent first viewport — it needs at minimum a name, a category and one route in. Every teardown in the set files the baked-in hero under 'avoid' for this project. So: eyebrow, the mark, one line, one button, all in the DOM, set over a clean plate — which is sapphire's pattern, minus its fragile per-slide text-shadow.

SCRIM — none versus a flat tint versus a gradient. None: sanasafinaz, mariab, naushemian, khaadi (the photograph runs at full strength and all type is inside the JPEG, so no scrim is needed). Flat tint: HSY (#000 at 0.3). Per-slide, inconsistent: amiradnan (0.2 on slide 2 only, none on the other three). Text-shadow only: sapphire (2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.4), and slide 3 has the class commented out, so any photo swap can break contrast silently). CALL: ONE BOTTOM-ANCHORED GRADIENT, rgba(14,14,15,.72) at 0% to transparent by 55%, and image opacity restored to 1. The sites that need no scrim are the sites with no HTML type over the image; the moment you put live copy on a photograph you owe it a guaranteed contrast floor, and sapphire proves a text-shadow is not one. But the scrim belongs where the type is. The current page does the opposite: 78% black over empty sky at the top and near-nothing at the bottom where the copy actually sits, plus a blanket opacity:.55 on the image on top of that.

CAROUSEL AND AUTOPLAY — three positions. Autoplay on: amiradnan (7s, 4 slides), ismailfarid (5s, 7 slides, with data-arrows and data-dots both false so 0 arrows and 0 dots exist in the DOM — 35 seconds to cycle and six of seven collection entry points unreachable on purpose), republic (5s, 10 slides), mariab (10s, 6 slides). Autoplay off: naushemian (33 slides, slideShow:false, so almost every visitor sees exactly one image and 32 preloaded files are dead weight), khaadi (data-autoplay=false, 3 slides, dots only), sapphire (autoplay:false, 3 slides). CALL: NO CAROUSEL AT ALL. ONE STATIC PLATE. Five pieces do not need six slides. Naushemian's 33-slides-with-autoplay-off and Ismail Farid's 7-slides-with-no-controls are both waste in opposite directions, and khaadi's own teardown notes the deeper reason a carousel is unnecessary: its desktop hero is a triptych — three portrait photographs butted edge to edge inside one 1920x700 file — delivering three looks in one banner-height slot. If Lada ever needs to show more than one look above the fold, do that instead of adding a slide.

PRODUCT CARD RATIO — 2:3 versus 13:16 versus 1200x1580 versus 0.652. 2:3 camp: sanasafinaz, mariab, khaadi, naushemian (all womenswear or bridal-led). republic: 13:16 = 0.812. ismailfarid: 1200x1580 = 0.759. HSY: 0.652, taller than 2:3. Current Lada: 4:5 = 0.800. CALL: KEEP 4:5 FOR THE GRID AND THE PDP, USE 2:3 FOR THE LOOKBOOK ONLY. This is a deliberate deviation from the set's most common number and the reason is the garment. A waistcoat is a torso piece that ends at the hip; HSY's 0.652 and the 2:3 camp are cut for a floor-length sherwani or bridal silhouette where the hem is the bottom of the frame. Ismail Farid is the closest analogue in the entire set — a Pakistani menswear house shooting waistcoats and eastern blazers — and it sits at 0.759. 4:5 sits between Ismail Farid and Republic, crops a waistcoat at mid-thigh where the garment's story actually ends, and is already what .pcard__media declares, so the CSS does not move. The rule to import is not the number, it is the enforcement: one ratio, held everywhere, shot to the crop.

object-fit CONTAIN VERSUS COVER. contain: ismailfarid (the garment is never cropped, it is letterboxed instead — the PDP main image is 425px inside a 585px column with about 80px of white each side, and the teardown counts this as a premium device). fill: khaadi (safe only because box and source ratios match exactly today, and flagged because the first mis-sized upload distorts a garment rather than cropping it). cover: everyone else. CALL: COVER, AND ENFORCE THE RATIO AT CAPTURE. Ismail Farid can afford contain because it holds 93.3% single-ratio compliance across 3,393 images; Lada has one photographer and five pieces, so the discipline belongs in the shoot brief, not in a fallback that letterboxes. Never fill.

PRICE — shown openly versus withheld into an enquiry. Shown: naushemian (₨22,500-195,000 across waistcoats with no 'price on request' coyness, which keeps the configurator's add-on maths legible), republic, sapphire, mariab, sanasafinaz's ready-to-wear. Withheld: HSY (89 of 250 variants at 0.00, plus a belt-and-braces .price__container{display:none} on all 12 homepage sections, with 'Price on Request' itself being the wa.me link on 16 of 16 menswear cards). Two-tier: ismailfarid (ready-to-wear priced, sized and add-to-cart, while all 97 sherwanis and 31 of 43 western grooms-wear pieces replace the price with 'Inquire now at online@ismailfarid.com' and hide both add-to-cart and the size selector — one template, two commercial models), sanasafinaz (couture cards drop the title for a bare reference code and swap Quick Add for an outline VIEW DETAILS). CALL: TWO-TIER, ISMAIL FARID'S MODEL. Show the price on standard 38R-46R waistcoats and coats; replace it with 'Measured in the shop' routing to WhatsApp on made-to-measure. Khan Jee is a shop with a counter, not a couture atelier — withholding the price on a Rs.19,990 waistcoat reads as evasive, and Maria.B.'s menswear waistcoats at Rs.15,490-19,990 with no discount are the honest comparison. But the measurement service genuinely has no list price, so it gets HSY's treatment.

FILTERS AND SORT — none versus full facets. None: republicwomenswear (all 100 collections have empty body_html and the page has no title, breadcrumb, filter, sort, count or pagination — one rule kills them all; tolerable at 15 SKUs, unusable beyond), ismailfarid (zero facets on a 109-product collection, only a sort dropdown, and the results count is rendered then hidden with inline display:none), HSY (price_range, sort_by and availability appear zero times — 'fine at 19 waistcoats, actively hostile at 93 menswear pieces'). Full: khaadi (8 dimensions, every long facet truncated to exactly 6 values then Show More, live result counts inline, colour as real circular swatches and fabric as plain text, a dual min/max price slider, and an INLINE 300px left rail that reflows the grid rather than covering it). CALL: NO FACET RAIL NOW — a scrollable sub-category pill row instead (Maria.B.'s collection-page pill pattern, at radius 0 rather than 6px). At five to thirteen pieces a facet drawer is furniture pretending to be depth. Revisit above about 30 SKUs, and when you do, copy Khaadi's exact pattern, because Amir Adnan's teardown names the win: for waistcoats, colour and occasion facets are the single biggest available improvement.

DESKTOP NAVIGATION — hamburger everywhere versus a visible bar. Hamburger at every breakpoint: mariab (<header-drawer data-breakpoint="desktop">, so the entire taxonomy sits behind one hamburger and the header holds only a centred logo and four icons — nothing competes with the image), ismailfarid (a 29-item inline menu exists in the DOM but computes visible:false at 1440px, which its teardown flags as a defect: 91 collections behind a hamburger on a wide screen). Visible bar: amiradnan (199px tall, non-sticky, two wrapped nav rows consuming 19vh and then scrolling away — also flagged), republic, khaadi, sapphire. CALL: FOR THIS ONE PAGE, a transparent header over the plate carrying the Khan Jee mark and the icons, going solid --lada-ground on scroll — Maria.B.'s pattern minus the per-slide recolouring, which a single static plate does not need (just set --header-content-color to --lada-bone for this template). Do not adopt Ismail Farid's hamburger-at-1440 for the wider site, and do not adopt Amir Adnan's 199px non-sticky block that consumes a fifth of the viewport and then abandons the visitor for 8,000px.

WHAT IDENTIFIES A PIECE ON THE CARD — proper name versus descriptor-spec versus reference code. Proper names: HSY (Dewaan, Zafraan, Zarmaan, Shamsher, Nawab-e-Zar, Gulrukh — every garment has one, and navigation is organised by named story collection first with garment type only as the secondary axis), naushemian (named collections). Descriptor-spec: khaadi ('Teal Cambric Pants' — colour plus fabric plus garment, strictly descriptive, no poetic naming at all, and it works because both halves of the eyebrow are real filter dimensions), sanasafinaz ('Stitched Printed Lawn Shirt+ Culotte' — pure construction spec with identity pushed to the SKU), mariab (raw catalogue strings, which its own teardown flags: 'a spec, not a name'). Reference code: sanasafinaz's couture tier (R-114, no descriptive title at all). CALL: PROPER NAME PLUS KHAADI'S EYEBROW. A named piece with a 'cloth | cut' line above it — 'Boski | Band collar' over 'Shamsher'. And no SKU on the visible card: Naushemian is criticised for 'SEQUINS EMBELLISHED MENS WAISTCOAT – NA-WC130' in the h3 and Maria.B. for printing 'MBM-WCSS26-18-Concrete-Small' under the H1. Note this collides with the existing rule in snippets/product-card.liquid, which surfaces the KJC SKU in place of a supplier name — that rule exists to hide a supplier, and Lada has none, so on the Lada card the SKU line becomes the cloth line. That is why the card should be forked rather than restyled.

DENSITY TOGGLE — ship one or not. Shipped: mariab (three modes; gridView-3 goes to 8-up at 12.5% and strips the card to a bare image tile by hiding .card__content, .card__badge and the hover bar), sapphire (grid-view-6 sets .product-tile-element{display:none!important} and collapses gutters to 2px), khaadi (four desktop options, active state an 8px 1px underline). CALL: NO TOGGLE. It is a genuinely good idea — an explicit browse-as-lookbook mode — and it is the wrong idea for five products, where the densest mode would produce one row. The lookbook section delivers the same 'just show me the clothes' payoff at Lada's scale.
keep_from_current: THE MARK AS ARTWORK RATHER THAN TYPE, loaded eagerly, wrapped in the page's only h1, with a real screen-reader label passed through the schema ('This is the name a screen reader reads out' — the comment in lada-band.liquid). Nothing in the study set does better and several do worse: naushemian and ismailfarid both ship raster logos (ismailfarid's is a JPEG, ismail-farid-logo_200x.jpg, flagged for not being SVG or transparent PNG), HSY sets its entire couture heading register in Times New Roman, and naushemian specifies Lora for every product title without ever loading it. Do not replace the gold-gradient lockup with type.

LIVE HTML COPY IN THE HERO. Seven of nine sites bake every hero word into the JPEG and all nine teardowns file it under 'avoid' for this project. This is the current page's single best decision and the redesign must not trade it away in pursuit of a silent plate.

THE prefers-reduced-motion BLOCK AT kj-v2.css:306-309, and the reasoning written above it — a 22s scale on a full-bleed image is exactly the large-area movement that triggers vestibular symptoms. The animation itself should go; the guard should stay and cover the card hover and the scroll reveals instead. Note that sanasafinaz, mariab and sapphire all ship substantial motion and none of the teardowns records a reduced-motion guard anywhere in the set.

THE QUICK-ADD FIX AND THE REASONING ALREADY IN THE CSS: hover-reveal on pointer devices so the photograph stays clean, and a permanent 44px target in the card's own flow on anything without hover. Sana Safinaz gets exactly this wrong — its Quick Add reveal is gated at min-width:1025px, so on tablet a black bar sits permanently across the bottom of every product photograph. Amir Adnan gets it right the harder way, hard-disabling both hover affordances on touch via .supports-touch{display:none}. Lada's version is better than both because it substitutes a real touch affordance rather than removing one.

THE WARM NEAR-BLACK GROUND. #0E0E0F is not #000, and that is the same instinct the teardowns credit in khaadi (#2d2b2a, 'never pure black', with a warm three-step grey ladder doing all the hierarchy work) and amiradnan (#1a1a1a ink on #faf8f5). The register is fixed anyway, but it is worth knowing it is right rather than merely mandated.

RADIUS 0 AND NO SHADOWS, already locked in the project tokens. That matches five of nine sites, and the two exceptions are the two the teardowns call out: sapphire's 10px radius on 40px Bootstrap pills ('reads mass-market, not tailoring') and mariab's 4-to-12px ladder. HSY's zero-radius, hairline, shadowless chrome is the closest match to where Lada already is.

--fs-micro AT 11px AS THE SINGLE MICRO SIZE, and the note explaining why (the values it replaced ran from 9.6px to 10.88px). The set is full of type below the legibility floor: naushemian ships widget titles at 10px, sapphire ships SKU lines at 10px and tile subtitles at 10px, amiradnan sets its announcement bar at 9.75px. One micro size at 11px, once, is better practice than any of them.

THE 38R-46R TABLE WITH REAL INCH MEASUREMENTS AND THE FOUR HOW-TO-MEASURE LINES ('Measure over a shirt, not bare skin', 'Chest: the fullest point, tape level under the arms'). Only naushemian and sapphire in the entire set ship a genuine garment measurement table; amiradnan, ismailfarid and HSY ship none at all and are flagged for it. This is already better than five of nine sites — it needs more columns, an INCHES/CM toggle and a second entry point beside the size selector, not a rebuild.

THE UNCONDITIONAL GUARANTEE AND THE FREE IN-SHOP MEASUREMENT. Nothing in the study set can claim either. HSY sells a 60-minute appointment through Calendly; naushemian charges nothing for 'My Custom Size' but asks for 12-15 days; ismailfarid replaces the price of 97 sherwanis with an email address. A no-conditions replacement promise plus measuring at the counter at no cost is a genuinely differentiated offer and it is currently compressed into a hero seal reading 'Replaced or refunded, no conditions.' Promote it, do not dilute it.

THE WHATSAPP ROUTES WITH PRE-FILLED MESSAGE TEXT (the reserve link in lada-collection and the sizing link, both url_encode'd). Republic routes three separate numbers by intent — online pret orders, bridal-studio appointments, bridal orders — and HSY makes 'Price on Request' itself the wa.me link on every menswear card. Pre-filling the message so the customer does not have to explain themselves is a refinement none of the nine bothers with. Keep it, and split it two ways by intent.

THE EMPTY STATE THAT SELLS RATHER THAN APOLOGISES ('Arriving this season / The new Lada range is on the looms. Reserve a piece, or ask for the line list, and we will hold it for you.'). Republic has the same instinct on stock-outs — sold-out pieces stay in the grid at full brightness under a 35% black centre band, still clickable, sorted to the end, and the PDP degrades into a 'NOTIFY WHEN AVAILABLE' capture. Keep the Lada empty state; retarget the copy from cloth to garments.

THE SECTION SCHEMA DISCIPLINE. Every string on the page is a merchandiser-editable setting with a sane default, and the size table and promise lists are pipe-delimited settings rather than hard-coded markup. Two of the nine are explicitly damaged by the opposite: sapphire ships nine separate merchandiser-authored <style> blocks inside the hero alone, redefining heading classes and forcing font-size with !important from CMS copy fields, and khaadi's Page Designer editors inline style="color: black" and <strong> into section headings so an h2 the CSS specifies at 24px/w500/uppercase/-1px actually renders at 42px/w900/sentence-case/+1px. Lada's content layer is already constrained to named settings. Keep it that way.
spec.typography: MONTSERRAT ONLY, AND THE INFRASTRUCTURE IS ALREADY CORRECT — theme/assets/fonts.css self-hosts it as a variable face at font-weight:100 900 across two subsets, so every weight specified below actually renders and the page costs two font requests rather than eight. That single fact puts Lada ahead of four of the nine sites on execution: amiradnan loads Poppins at 400 only and then asks for 700 on every button, so every bold on a premium site is browser-synthesised; ismailfarid requests font-weight:200 on its collection H2 when only 400/500/600/700 are loaded, so the intended hairline silently substitutes to 400, and asks 700 of a single-weight Whitney face; naushemian specifies Lora for every product-card title and never loads it at all, so titles fall back to MS Sans Serif; sapphire specifies weight 300 on its editorial descriptions with only 400-700 @font-face'd. Sana Safinaz is the cautionary tale in the other direction — two geometric sans (Quicksand and Outfit) so near-identical in voice that the DOM carries no hierarchy at all, which is precisely why all its brand character had to be moved into the JPEGs. Montserrat single-family is Maria.B.'s model (--font-body-family and --font-heading-family both resolve to it) and it works there for the same reason it will work here: the photography carries the register.  ///  SCALE, and it is deliberately short. Micro caps: 11px (the existing --fs-micro), weight 600, letter-spacing 0.24em, uppercase — for eyebrows, kickers, seal labels, table headers, buttons and the card cloth line. Body and lede: 15px, weight 300, line-height 1.75, max-width 60ch for prose and 48ch for the lede. Card piece name: 15px, weight 500, sentence case, letter-spacing 0. Card price: 15px, weight 500, tabular-nums, the SAME size as the name, never larger, never coloured. PDP h1: 22px, weight 500. Section h2: clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem) — 28px to 40px — weight 500, letter-spacing -0.01em, line-height 1.08, sentence case. Nothing on the page exceeds 40px of type. The largest thing on the page is the mark, which is artwork, and the second largest is a section h2; the current hero's clamp(3.4rem,12vw,8rem) wordmark fallback and the 3.2rem h2 ceiling are both above that and are what make the page read as a poster. This ceiling is republicwomenswear's discipline taken one step less far (nothing above 18px there, which is too far for a page that has to carry live copy), amiradnan's 32px scale cap, and mariab's 32px section h2 with a 20px product h1.  ///  TRACKING IS THE MAIN FIX. Two values on the whole page: 0.24em on the 11px micro caps, and 0 on everything else — body, lede, h2, h3, card names, prices, table cells. The current Lada block ships seven (.36em, .32em, .28em, .26em, .24em, .22em, .16em) and nothing at 0, so no tracked element reads as a decision. This is Ismail Farid's rule stated plainly — tracking hoarded, not sprayed, spent on exactly two elements so those two read as deliberate — reinforced by sapphire (normal on hero and all body, reserved for 40-45px headings) and mariab (h1-h5 at letter-spacing:0, line-height:100%). Khaadi's inverse move, negative tracking at -1px on 24px and -2px on 32px display type, is the set's most distinctive typographic fingerprint but it belongs to a proprietary face; Montserrat at -0.01em on the h2 is as far as that should be pushed.  ///  CASE: uppercase only at 11px micro, via text-transform in CSS and never by typing capitals into a content field. Naushemian and sanasafinaz both type their capitals into the CMS, which is exactly how SKU codes end up inside customer-facing headings. Section h2s and piece names are sentence case.  ///  CONTRAST — one measured correction. --lada-muted #8B8579 on --lada-ground #0E0E0F is about 5.6:1 and passes, so body copy is fine as it stands, but the page currently drops to --text-tertiary #6B615A on that ground in the borrowed product card (about 2.6:1) and sets 0.86rem/0.9rem body at that weight in several places. Fix the card by using --lada-muted for secondary text and --lada-bone for anything a customer must read, and never go below 13px for a full sentence. This is Ismail Farid's exact failure — card title and price both at #AFAFAE on white, roughly 2.2:1 against a 4.5:1 floor — where the teardown's own remedy is the right one: keep the recessive intent, correct the value.  ///  ONE H1 PER PAGE, on the mark. Four of the nine ship no h1 at all (amiradnan's collection pages, mariab's homepage, republic's two empty h1 elements that still consume 47px and 10px of vertical space, HSY's only h1 being class=\"visually-hidden\"). Lada already gets this right in lada-hero.liquid — protect it, and make sure the section h2s below it are h2s in document order.
interactions: DELETE THE HERO KEN BURNS. Remove the ladaZoom keyframe and its animation on .lada__hero img; keep the prefers-reduced-motion block and repoint it at the card hover and the scroll reveals. Not one of the nine sites animates its hero plate — mariab, khaadi, sanasafinaz and naushemian all hold a still image. Sana Safinaz's entire motion budget is four centralised tokens (--duration-short .1s through --duration-long .5s) with 'nothing bespoke, nothing bouncy'. A 22s full-bleed scale is the one place Lada spends more motion than any site in the study set.

CARD HOVER: ISMAIL FARID'S EXACT CURVE. Cross-fade to the second frame over 0.5s while the incoming image continues to scale(1.05) over a full 2s on cubic-bezier(0,0,.44,1.18) — the y2 of 1.18 carries it past 1.05 before it settles, so the card is still breathing long after the swap finishes. Both images position:absolute in an overflow:hidden box. Sapphire runs the identical curve at scale(1.09). The current .pcard is close (opacity .6s, transform 1.3s on --ease, scale 1.045) but linear-ish easing on a 1.3s scale reads as a UI transition rather than a photograph settling. Import the overshoot.

THE HOVER PAIR IS CONTENT, NOT DECORATION, AND THE SHOOT MUST SUPPLY IT. Frame 1 is the three-quarter torso-to-mid-thigh crop; frame 2 is the full head-to-toe standing figure from the same set, same light, same model. Ismail Farid's teardown is explicit that this is what makes the swap worth having: hover answers 'what does the whole thing look like on', which is the exact question a waistcoat shopper has. Naushemian's rule is the same in the negative — the hover image is 'always a second model frame, never a detail or flat shot'. Today Lada has no second frame for any piece, so the hover fires against nothing.

KEEP THE TOUCH SUBSTITUTION, DO NOT LEAVE A PHANTOM HOVER. On pointer devices the quick-add slides up over the bottom of the photograph and the resting grid stays pure photography (sanasafinaz parks it at translateY(100%) below the image edge, naushemian at bottom:-40px with visibility:hidden, mariab at bottom:-15%). On anything without hover it becomes a permanent 44px target in the card's own flow — which the current CSS already does, and which Sana Safinaz fails at by gating its reveal at min-width:1025px so a black bar sits permanently across every tablet photograph. Amir Adnan's blunter fix (.supports-touch{display:none} on both hover affordances) is also acceptable; a phantom hover state is not.

LOOKBOOK: CSS SCROLL-SNAP, NEVER WHEEL CAPTURE. scroll-snap-type: y proximity on the container, scroll-snap-align: start on each frame. Sana Safinaz's homepage is a vertical Swiper with mousewheel releaseOnEdges:false, so one gesture equals exactly one full-screen plate and the page physically cannot be scrolled past — and its own teardown recommends scroll-snap as the replacement, because the capture breaks find-in-page, deep-linking to a panel, keyboard and trackpad users. Proximity rather than mandatory so a visitor can still stop between frames.

ROW GAP FAR EXCEEDING COLUMN GAP IN THE GRID. Target roughly 4:1 — column-gap var(--s4), row-gap var(--s8). Maria.B. runs column-gap 20px against row-gap 96px, 4.8x, so rows read as separate editorial spreads rather than a table of stock; Ismail Farid runs gapX 30px against gapY 60px, exactly double. The current .pgrid is s6/s4 then s7/s5 — close to 1.3:1, which reads as a catalogue table.

THE UNDERLINE THAT COMPLETES ITSELF, for 'The full range' and any secondary text link. A ::before at width:50%, height:1px, bottom:-8px, anchored right, growing to width:100% on hover over 0.3s — so the rule finishes rather than changing colour. Maria.B.'s .tr-viewAll-btn. Pair it with Maria.B.'s arrow nudge on the primary CTA: the SVG translateX(10px) on hover while the button itself does not move. Amir Adnan's quieter variant is also good and cheaper — a title underline at text-underline-offset:.3rem, no colour change, no box, no shift.

MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ACCORDIONS WITH NO JAVASCRIPT. <details name="lada-info"> on the promise section's two panels and on the PDP's Cloth/Care panels — the HTML name attribute makes opening one close the other natively. Maria.B. Draw them as 1px hairlines with +/- indicators, no card, no shadow, no fill (khaadi: 'the PDP information architecture is drawn entirely with lines'). Closed by default.

SIZE GUIDE AS AN INLINE POPOVER BESIDE THE SIZE SELECTOR, not only as a page section and never only in the footer. Naushemian triggers a real measurement table from a link next to the size select — measurement help at the exact moment of doubt. Amir Adnan is the counter-example: zero size-chart matches anywhere on the PDP, with the Size Guide link living only in the footer. Same markup as lada-sizing, two entry points.

SCROLL REVEAL, STAGGERED, ONCE. opacity .01 to 1 with translateY(2rem) to 0 over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0,0,.3,1), staggered about 75ms per item via a --animation-order custom property on each grid child. Maria.B.'s scroll-trigger animate--slide-in; HSY ships the same Dawn pattern with inline --animation-order 1..8 per card and no library. Guard it with the existing reduced-motion block.

NO CAROUSELS ANYWHERE ON THIS PAGE. One product grid and one editorial run, full stop. The set's clearest structural failure is repetition: Amir Adnan ships four near-identical featured-collection rows at 616/719/704/919px, 2,958px of homepage that all reads the same and is 'a category index dressed as a homepage'; HSY ships six near-identical carousel rows back to back with no editorial break, and then ships each of them twice as separate desktop and mobile DOM sections toggled with display:none on a 796KB page; naushemian ships four 4-up product grids in a row. Lada has five pieces — one grid is the honest presentation.

ONE PERSISTENT WHATSAPP LAUNCHER, ON-REGISTER. Fixed bottom-right, champagne on ground, radius 0, 44px minimum. Ismail Farid, republic and HSY all run one and it suits an enquiry-led funnel. HSY's is also the styling warning: a teal #26a69a bubble at border-radius 2px dropped into an otherwise strict black-and-white zero-radius system. Do not let a third-party widget set a colour or a radius the page does not already have — the same failure produces Amir Adnan's #6016eb purple BNPL widget on every card and its 12px/14px/8px radii against a 0px site-wide contract.

HEADER: TRANSPARENT OVER THE PLATE, SOLID ON SCROLL. Set --header-content-color to --lada-bone for this template so the mark and icons read against the photograph, then flip to a solid --lada-ground background on .scrolled-past-header. Maria.B. does this and additionally recolours per slide from a data-header-color attribute, which one static plate makes unnecessary. Sticky is not optional: khaadi's filter rail is position:static and scrolls away entirely (measured top -988 after a 1400px scroll), amiradnan's 199px header is non-sticky so navigation is unreachable for the remaining 8,000px, and republic's header is position:static with a full-page cart, so every add-to-cart throws the customer out of the collection.

PDP GALLERY: A CONTACT SHEET, NOT A SLIDESHOW. Show every frame at once in a 2-up grid at 4:5 with a 4px gutter and no thumbnail rail, both columns position:sticky. Sapphire (8/12 gallery as a 2-up flex-wrap grid, all six images visible, 4px padding) and sanasafinaz (media-gallery--two-column, 8 images all rendered, --image-gap:4px, --media-radius:0px) both do this, and the register it creates is a contact sheet rather than a click-through. Add a click-to-open full-resolution lightbox (mariab wraps each slide in a Fancybox anchor at width=3200). Avoid Republic's inversion, where the main product photograph renders at 435x535 — the same size as a grid card, 30% of the width — on a site whose entire premium claim is the photography.

QUANTITY: A STEPPER CAPPED AT 2 OR 3. Khaadi ships a quantity dropdown running 1 to 50 on a single kurta, and its teardown names the cost exactly: it reads wholesale, not atelier. For a Sheikhupura-cut waistcoat a low cap says made in small numbers.

imagery_brief.subject: One male model, mid-30s, standing three-quarter turn to camera, weight on the back foot, hands relaxed — not hand-on-hip. Wearing a Lada waistcoat over a plain kurta and shalwar, styled head to toe including shoes. Framed waist-up-plus, roughly knee to just above the head, model placed in the RIGHT two-thirds of the frame with the left third held quiet and low-detail for the eyebrow, mark and lede to sit over. Location: a warm plaster or old brick wall, a carved wooden door, or a shaded arcade in Sheikhupura — real architecture, no studio.
imagery_brief.ratio: 3:2 landscape. Deliver 2880x1920 master, serve 1440w/2880w. Set the width and height attributes to the TRUE intrinsic dimensions — the current section hard-codes 2400x1500 over a 1000x1250 file.
imagery_brief.treatment: Late-afternoon side light, one direction, no fill flash. Warm grade, shadows kept open rather than crushed, so the frame sits against #0E0E0F without a hard edge. NO opacity reduction and NO overall tint — the only overlay is a bottom-anchored gradient from rgba(14,14,15,.72) at 0% to transparent by 55%, so the type has a contrast floor and the top two-thirds of the photograph runs at full strength. Garment tone should differ from the wall tone by at least two stops so the waistcoat's silhouette reads at a glance. Two separately art-directed uploads, not one file re-cropped by CSS: ismailfarid ships 1440x551 desktop and 640x960 mobile as distinct files, khaadi ships a 1920x700 triptych and a different 1000x1500 portrait, sapphire swaps 2:1 and 4:5 via <picture><source media>. Amir Adnan's failure is the reason: one padding-bottom:56.25% rule in both media queries gives a 90vh desktop hero and a 26vh letterboxed strip at 375px.

imagery_brief.subject: Same model, same garment, same location and same session — but recomposed, not cropped. Tighter: chest to head, turned slightly further into the light, with the waistcoat's front closure and collar band clearly legible at small size. Quiet area at the BOTTOM third for type, since the mobile plate stacks its copy under the figure.
imagery_brief.treatment: Identical grade to the desktop plate so the two read as one shoot. Because the copy sits low, the gradient runs from rgba(14,14,15,.8) at 0% to transparent by 62%. Do not simply object-fit:cover the landscape master — Sana Safinaz's teardown shows what that costs: a 16:9 source in a 100vh frame centre-crops about 10% vertically and it is the baked-in text at the edges that gets clipped.

imagery_brief.subject: Per piece. Single male model, three-quarter turn, cropped from just above the head to MID-THIGH — the waistcoat's hem, the shalwar's fall and the hands all in frame. Model styled head to toe. Front closure, collar band and pocket line all readable. One model across the whole range so the grid reads as one shoot.
imagery_brief.ratio: 4:5 (0.800). Master 1600x2000, srcset 400/800/1200/1600w, object-fit:cover into an aspect-ratio:4/5 box.
imagery_brief.treatment: On location or on a built set with a tonal background chosen to harmonise with the garment and sit low-contrast against it — ismailfarid's exact method (off-white waistcoat in open desert against blown-out pale sky; maroon monogram waistcoat in an atelier interior of stacked painters' canvases and a period wooden chair). Never a white sweep, never a flat-lay, never a ghost mannequin: khaadi's most consistent decision across its whole catalogue is that every product image has a human in it. Warm, single-source natural light. Placeholder box behind the image must be --lada-panel #17171A, not the light theme's --surface #FAF8F6.

imagery_brief.subject: Per piece, SAME set, same light, same model, same session as card-primary. Full head-to-toe standing figure, feet near the bottom edge of the frame, front-on or a shallow three-quarter. This frame's only job is to answer 'what does the whole thing look like on'.
imagery_brief.ratio: 4:5, 1600x2000, identical to card-primary so the cross-fade has no reframe.
imagery_brief.treatment: Identical grade and background to card-primary — the hover must change the information, not the register. Ismail Farid's shot sequence is the model to copy exactly: frame 1 a three-quarter mid-thigh-up crop, frame 2 the full standing figure, and the card hover is nothing but that pair. Naushemian's rule is the same stated negatively — the hover frame is always a second model frame, never a detail or a flat.

imagery_brief.subject: Per piece, two to three frames. Construction evidence at close range, no model face: the buttonhole and button (bone, brass or self-covered) at roughly life size; the bone-lip or welt pocket corner; the collar band where it meets the shoulder seam; the lining and the internal facing shown by holding the front open. Hands may appear. For any embroidered or brocade piece, one frame of the thread work at 1:1.
imagery_brief.ratio: 4:5, FULL FRAME — same 1600x2000 box as the card and the PDP gallery. Not a square, not an inset, not a thumbnail.
imagery_brief.treatment: Raking side light to reveal weave and stitch depth; shallow depth of field with the stitch line as the plane of focus. Republic's discipline is the point: its macro detail frames (lace hem, tilla embroidery, laser cutwork) are delivered at the same full 13:16 portrait frame as the model shots, so the craftsmanship shot gets the same real estate. The set's gap makes the case — Amir Adnan has almost no macro at all (median 3 images per product means three near-identical poses rather than a pose plus a weave close-up), and naushemian is criticised for shipping only 2 gallery images on a ₨95,000 made-to-order garment with nothing evidencing the embroidery being sold. Target 5 to 7 frames per Lada piece: primary, full-length, two to three macros, one back view.

imagery_brief.subject: The Sheikhupura workshop floor. Hands and forearms only, no face: chalk and a pattern card on cloth on the cutting table, shears mid-cut, the marked panel lifting away. Real table, real offcuts, real light through the shop window — not staged clean.
imagery_brief.treatment: Available light, warm, slightly underexposed so it reads as a working room rather than a set. Grade to match the garment photography. This is provenance photography, so resist styling it: the persuasive detail is the wear on the table.

imagery_brief.subject: A machinist at the needle plate, mid-seam, hands guiding the panel under the foot. Face optional and only with consent; if named, credit the maker in the copy. The needle, the thread cone and the seam allowance in focus.
imagery_brief.treatment: Same available-light, same grade. A slow enough shutter that the machine reads as running. Naushemian credits its karigars by name in the lookbook intro and HSY signs its homepage story in the first person as the founder — naming the person is what turns a process shot into provenance.

imagery_brief.subject: The pressing and the finishing: a heavy iron on the shoulder over a ham, steam visible; or the completed waistcoat on a wooden form or a hanger against the workshop wall, with the pocket line and hem falling correctly. No model.
imagery_brief.treatment: Same grade. One clean, resolved frame — this is the section's full stop, so it should be the calmest of the three.

imagery_brief.subject: Six frames, one per look, editorial rather than catalogue: the model seated on stone steps, walking through an arcade, standing in a doorway, half-turned against a painted wall, hands adjusting a cuff, a back view showing the waistcoat's rear seam and belt. Full-length or near it. Two of the six may include a second figure for scale and rhythm.
imagery_brief.ratio: 2:3 portrait, delivered at native camera resolution — 1707x2560 or larger, uncropped.
imagery_brief.treatment: This is the one place to loosen the grid: presented full-bleed and whole, as the photographer framed them, not art-directed into a card. Zero captions, zero prices, zero badges. Three of the six get wrapped in a bare product link with no visible affordance. Naushemian's /farhaad-2026 is the exact reference — 33 portrait frames at 1707x2560 served uncropped with EXIF intact, no commerce signal anywhere on the page, and 6 frames quietly wrapped in <a href="/product/…">.

imagery_brief.subject: Two frames, wider and quieter, to break the portrait run: the model small in a large architectural space; or a horizontal detail — a row of finished coats on a rail, the shopfront's inner arch, cloth bolts stacked. These carry no garment sell, only register.
imagery_brief.treatment: Same grade as the portraits. Full-bleed, no caption. Naushemian mixes 8 landscape frames at 2560x1707 into its 33 portraits for exactly this rhythm. Important: these two frames MUST have a mobile counterpart or be dropped below 750px — Republic's two full-bleed 32:15 banners collapse to 23px and 83px tall on a 375px phone, unreadable slivers that still load full-size files.

imagery_brief.subject: The measuring itself, at the shop counter. Hands and a cloth tape across a customer's chest over a shirt, or the tape draped over the tailor's shoulder beside a notebook of measurements. No faces. Include one recognisable piece of the shop — the counter edge, a bolt of cloth, the brass rule.
imagery_brief.treatment: Warm interior light, slightly high angle looking down at the tape and the notebook. This frame has to say 'a person does this for you in a room', which is the whole differentiator. Do not stage it with a suited stylist; the credible version is the shop as it is.

imagery_brief.subject: Khan Jee Center, Civil Quarters Road, Sheikhupura — the actual shopfront, exterior, at dusk with the interior lights on so the shop reads as open and occupied. Signage legible. Street context visible but not busy.
imagery_brief.treatment: Blue-hour exposure balanced for the warm interior, so the doorway glows against a cool street. This is the 1978 claim made visible, and it is the single asset in this brief that none of the nine studied sites can match with art direction — Ismail Farid, Republic, Naushemian and HSY all assert their physical premises in plain footer text precisely because it is the strongest trust signal available.

imagery_brief.subject: NOT a photograph. A line drawing of a Lada waistcoat, front elevation, drawn at 1px in --lada-champagne #C6A15B on transparent, with six measurement callouts on hairline leader lines: chest, waist, length from collar base, shoulder, collar, armhole. A second smaller elevation of a coat beside it.
imagery_brief.ratio: 4:5, delivered as inline SVG so it inherits the champagne token and stays crisp at any size.
imagery_brief.treatment: Hairlines only, no fills, no shadow, no radius — consistent with khaadi's line-drawn information architecture. Sapphire pairs exactly this kind of garment technical drawing with its INCHES/CM tabbed table of seven measurements, and its teardown calls that the correct model for eastern silhouettes where fit is cut-specific. Sits beside the 38R-46R table and inside the PDP size popover.

imagery_brief.slot: DELIVERY RULES FOR EVERY SLOT ABOVE
imagery_brief.subject: Production constraints that apply across the whole shoot, not a picture.
imagery_brief.ratio: Two ratios only on the entire page: 4:5 for everything in the commerce flow (card, hover, macro, PDP gallery, craft) and 2:3 or 3:2 for editorial (lookbook, hero, measure, house). Shoot to the crop; never re-crop one master into a different box.
imagery_brief.treatment: WEBP or well-compressed JPEG, never PNG for photography — Amir Adnan ships 308 PNGs out of 962 catalogue images, including two waistcoat files at 1.8MB and 2.3MB at 1080px. Ship 2x for anything decorative: khaadi's mega-menu editorial image is a 370x360 natural file upscaled to 389px and its collection circles are 80x80 at 80px display, both visibly soft at dpr 2. No video anywhere on this page — HSY's hero MP4 has no poster frame, so first paint is an empty 75vh void until the file buffers, and Amir Adnan autoplays four 1080p/7.2Mbps reels on its homepage. Alt text written per image and never copy-pasted: naushemian's men's kurta card carries alt="Off-White Needleveil Ladies Dress with Striped Dupatta", and khaadi's hero alt is literally "Image Here". Print the fit reference in HTML next to the price ('Model is 5'11", wearing 40R'), not burned into the photograph — Amir Adnan burns it in bottom-right and the 2:3 card crop cuts off the right third, so it survives only on the PDP. Finally: do NOT source the architecture from stock. The Getty Hiran Minar images are off-limits on this project, and the licensed Hiran Minar photograph in use (Shaguftakarim, CC BY-SA 4.0) carries a footer credit obligation — Sheikhupura architecture shot for this brief avoids the question entirely and is more credible for a label that is actually made there.
